title: Minimum-weight nonzero codewords

problem.name: Minimum-weight nonzero codewords
problem.statement_latex: Given a full-rank generator matrix $G\in\mathbb F_2^{k\times n}$, output $u\ne0$ minimizing $|uG|$. The minimum value is the code's minimum distance. This is a discrete optimization problem related to syndrome decoding and the search for short dual codewords in statistical cryptanalysis. Complexity is measured in weight-oracle evaluations for the direct search, and quantum gates or classical bit operations for explicitly represented codes.

quantum.headline_latex: $O(2^{k/2})$ weight evaluations, D\"urr--H\o yer minimum finding; $C/\sqrt{p_w}$ for amplified ISD trials.
quantum.details_latex: The direct exact method has polynomial workspace and includes coherent computation of $uG$, its Hamming weight and comparison with a threshold. For random codes, let an ISD trial cost $C$ and find a nonzero word of weight at most $w$ with probability $p_w$. Amplification replaces the trial count by $O(p_w^{-1/2})$, and quantum nearest-neighbor walks can reduce the internal cost. Full attacks optimize weight, representations and list sizes.
quantum.headline_text: $O(2^{k/2})$ weight evaluations, Dürr–Høyer minimum finding; $C/\sqrt{p_w}$ for amplified ISD trials.

classical.headline_latex: The minimum of $O(2^k)$ weight evaluations, optimized ISD and applicable sparse-circuit counting.
classical.details_latex: Exhaustive enumeration can update codewords in Gray-code order. An ISD trial family gives expected work $C/p_w$, with optimized representations and nearest-neighbor matching improving the random-code comparator. If a generator or parity-check matrix has $s$ nonzero entries, the threshold predicate has $O(n+s)$ Boolean gates, yielding $\operatorname{poly}(n+s)2^{O((n+s)/\sqrt{\log(n+s)})}$ deterministic classical time. Binary search over the weight adds a polynomial factor. A linear-size representation gives subexponential time in $n$; dense constant-rate codes retain the stronger enumeration or ISD bound.

strength.description_latex: Polynomial speedup from quadratic acceleration of exhaustive weight search or a specified ISD success probability, giving a smaller exponential constant in the dense-code comparison.

evidence.description_latex: Rigorous oracle amplification; partial evidence for a full-runtime separation on explicit random codes. Sparse representations have the separate subexponential classical bound.

hardware.description_latex:
The direct circuit uses $k$ message qubits, $n$ codeword qubits, a weight register and polynomial ancillas. Exponentially many fault-tolerant repetitions dominate its cost. Faster quantum-walk variants use exponential coherent lists.

{\small [Before ``ETH is false'', the generic exact comparison was $O(2^k)$ classical weight evaluations versus $O(2^{k/2})$ quantum evaluations, a quadratic speedup also applied to sparse representations.]\par}
